senses: food made from offal (especially the lungs and heart)

entries: From Middle High German Diutschlant, compound word formed from phrasings like diutsch lant n, diutsche lant n, in diutscheme lande n, ze diutischeme lande n, (in) diutschiu lant n pl. The adjective deutsch is from Middle High German diutsc, diutisch, diutsch, tiutsch, tiusch, from Old High German diutisc (of the people). More at Dutchland.
senses: Germany (a nation or civilization occupying the country around the Rhine, Elbe, and upper Danube Rivers in Central Europe, taken as a whole under its various governments)
Germany (a country in Central Europe, formed in 1949 as West Germany, with its provisional capital Bonn until 1990, when it incorporated East Germany)
ellipsis of a nation state, the legal person comprising the most part of territory with German dominating, or its territory
ellipsis of Heiliges Römisches Reich Deutscher Nation or heiliges römisches Reich deutscher Nation

entries: 19th century, from Latin typhus, from Ancient Greek τῦφος (tûphos).
From Middle High German umberingen, from Old High German umbiringen, umbihringen, from Proto-West Germanic *umbihringan. By surface analysis, um- + Ring + -en. Compare Dutch omringen.
